A draft for the Nim forum

Draft · 10 November 2026

tabelline on the Nim forum

The post that announces tabelline 0.1 on the Nim forum: first as it will look, then the text to paste. Comment on it with ✎ Review.

Version 2 · updated 10 November 2026, after the first review

Title: tabelline: beautiful display tables for Nim · Category: Project Showcase. The two images are in this page's branch, linked by commit, so their addresses keep working after the merge.

The post

Hi, I just released tabelline 0.1, beautiful display tables for Nim:

https://github.com/pietroppeter/tabelline

It follows R's gt and Python's Great Tables: the same parts of a table and the same verbs in camelCase, written in plain Nim. Tables render to HTML, text and Markdown, and go straight into a nimib page. The name comes from le tabelline, the times tables of Italian primary school, and the idea from my friend Francesco.

Docs, with a Guide, a Book that ports the gt and Great Tables guides, and the roadmap: https://pietroppeter.github.io/tabelline/

As a small celebration I put every NimConf schedule, 2020 to 2026, in tabelline tables:

https://pietroppeter.github.io/claude-artifacts/nimconf-schedules/

That page also has a review mode for nimib pages: press ✎ Review, select some text, comment, and export all the comments to paste to a coding agent. How it works: https://pietroppeter.github.io/tabelline/devlog/review-mode/

Made with Claude, mostly from my phone. Feedback is welcome, especially from gt and Great Tables users.

The text to paste

Hi, I just released tabelline 0.1, beautiful display tables for Nim:

https://github.com/pietroppeter/tabelline

It follows R's [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com/) and Python's [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/): the same parts of a table and the same verbs in camelCase, written in plain Nim. Tables render to HTML, text and Markdown, and go straight into a nimib page. The name comes from *le tabelline*, the times tables of Italian primary school, and the idea from my friend Francesco.

To check before posting

  • Francesco: the post names him by first name only. Add his GitHub handle if he is happy to be tagged.
  • Images: the forum takes .. image:: url (reStructuredText). If it shows the line instead of the image, use a plain link.
  • Links: gt and Great Tables are Markdown links. If the forum shows the brackets, use bare URLs.
